newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOE's George sees inflation in Britain falling.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George sees inflation in Britain falling.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday he expected British inflation to decline in coming months and that there was a better or even chance of meeting government targets.

George declined to comment on whether he saw further need for a rise in interest rates, but added the BOE's view on interest rates would be contained in its monthly inflation report due for release on Tuesday.
"Wait until the inflation report, that will make it clear," George said in response to a question about another increase in interest rates.
George noted the "very strong appreciation of exchange rates" as a factor that would help Britain meet the inflation target.
George was speaking to reporters in Basle ahead of the monthly meeting of G10 central bank governors at the Bank for International Settlements.
"Our job is to achieve the the target of inflation that the government has set of 2-1/2 percent or less. There is a better or even chance of 2-1/2 percent or less," George added.
Asked whether he saw British inflation coming down within the next few months, George said: "Yes I do."
